translationRepairs: He then moved his own forces to Boxing.
He then moved his own forces to Boping.
s0014 reads 博平; with Dongchang, Shen, and the Grand Canal in the surrounding units this is Boping in Shandong, not Boxing (博興). The proposed replacement is accurate.
He himself moved the army to Boxing.
He himself moved the army to Boping.
The same focus unit has 博平; literal Boxing misidentifies the place. Boping restores the correct toponym without other changes.
Zhiwan stationed the army at Xuzhou; having dispatched various generals to set defenses, he himself led the army back to the provincial capital;
Zhiwan stationed the army at Xuchang; having dispatched various generals to set defenses, he himself led the army back to the provincial capital;
s0082 has 許州; Xuzhou would be 徐州. The idiomatic already has Xuchang, and s0083’s raid on 許 confirms the Henan prefecture. The proposed literal fix is correct.
In the fifteenth year of his reign he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and then transferred to the Eastern Pavilion.
In the fifteenth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Tiren Pavilion and then transferred to the Eastern Pavilion.

s0101 is only 十五年 after an established Guangxu sequence (s0099–s0100); ‘of his reign’ wrongly casts Zhang Zhiwan as the reigning emperor. Dropping that phrase matches the source and parallel year phrasing.
Britain incited the Gurkhas to war with Tibet, while the people of Dromo, ground down by harsh treatment from Tibetan officials, wished to submit to the Qing.
Britain incited the Gurkhas to war with Tibet, while the people of Zhantui, ground down by harsh treatment from Tibetan officials, wished to submit to the Qing.
s0129 has 瞻對; s0130 calls it 蜀門戶, which fits Zhantui/Nyarong on the Sichuan–Kham frontier, not Dromo/Chumbi. Zhantui is the accurate repair.
